limits: I cannot identify the material with confidence. The three significant peaks (155.7, 299.6, 354.1 cm-1) would need to be compared against a reference Raman library or literature mode table for layered candidates. None was available offline and I did not cite any literature values.

Above about 420 cm-1 no feature reaches 3 sigma. The noise is about 240 counts and the features are about 400-600 counts, so the weak bands at 478-1071 cm-1 that a naive peak search lists are consistent with noise plus background and are not reported as peaks.

The spectrum starts at 60 cm-1. Features at 70-190 cm-1 other than the 155.7 cm-1 peak are not significant (t≈2-3).
This is one unpolarized backscattering spectrum. No polarization dependence was measured, so no symmetry (irrep) or polarization pattern can be assigned to any peak.
Layer number, defect level and strain cannot be determined from these data.
The single-point spike at 897.47 cm-1 (9238 counts against neighbours of about 1500-1700) was replaced by the neighbour average before fitting. No other spikes were found at the 4.5-sigma level.
